issues.title: CSV column names incompatible with PyTorch
issues.description: Port writes NISQA_results.csv with columns [deg, mos, noi, dis, col, loud]. PyTorch writes [deg, mos_pred, noi_pred, dis_pred, col_pred, loud_pred] plus a 'model' column. Breaks downstream pipelines expecting PyTorch-compatible output.
issues.root_cause: predict.py _format_prediction uses output_names (mos, noi, ...) for both dict API and CSV columns.
issues.fix: Append '_pred' suffix to column names in CSV output; add 'model' column with checkpoint name.

issues.title: Persistent compilation cache non-functional
issues.description: load_model calls compilation_cache.initialize_cache() when cache_dir is passed, but the cache directory stays empty after multiple compiles. Cross-process cold-start compile (~0.88s) repeats every process restart. In-process cache works (130x).
issues.root_cause: Each load_model creates a new NisqaJaxModel with a fresh jax.jit closure. In-process XLA cache hits on program hash, but persistent disk cache is never populated.
issues.evidence: cache dir contents: [] after 3 compiles; speedup warm/cold = 1.06x
issues.fix: Set JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR env var before first jax import, or use jax.config.update('jax_compilation_cache_dir', path). Ensure the jit'd function is cacheable (stable closure).

issues.title: td_sa_nhead > 1 silently accepted but ignored
issues.description: model.py computes attention as single head (dim = d_model, scale 1/sqrt(d_model), no head reshape). PyTorch MultiheadAttention splits into nhead heads of d_model/nhead and scales by 1/sqrt(head_dim). For shipped checkpoints nhead=1 so exact. But config accepts any nhead without validating ==1 — a custom checkpoint with nhead=4 would load, run, and silently produce wrong results.
issues.root_cause: SelfAttention forward uses single-head path; config_from_checkpoint_args doesn't validate nhead==1.
issues.fix: Either validate td_sa_nhead==1 in config_from_checkpoint_args (reject nhead>1), or implement proper multi-head attention with head reshape and 1/sqrt(head_dim) scaling.

issues.title: TTS output named 'naturalness' vs PyTorch 'mos_pred'
issues.description: config.py sets output_names=('naturalness',) for nisqa_tts.tar, but PyTorch predict_mos always writes 'mos_pred'. TTS CSV column is 'naturalness', incompatible with PyTorch.
issues.fix: Use 'mos_pred' for CSV output; expose 'naturalness' as an optional alias in the dict API only.

issues.title: predict_batch([]) silently returns empty DataFrame
issues.description: Library API returns empty DataFrame with no error for empty path list, while CLI raises 'No wav files found'. Inconsistent failure mode.
issues.fix: Raise ValueError('No wav files provided') at start of predict_batch if len(wav_paths)==0.

issues.title: Stereo out-of-range channel gives misleading error
issues.description: predict_file(wav, channel=5) on stereo file raises 'Could not load file ...' — the IndexError from y[5,:] is caught and rewrapped as a load error. Raises (good) but message doesn't mention the bad channel.
issues.fix: Check channel against y.shape[0] before indexing; raise ValueError with channel-specific message.

issues.title: TF32 matmul precision never enabled on GPU
issues.description: Model __post_init__ wraps forward in jax.default_matmul_precision('float32') unconditionally. TF32 is safe for these small matmuls (drift=0.0000 measured) but never enabled, leaving tensor-core throughput on the table on Ampere+.
issues.fix: Add precision='tf32' option that uses jax.default_matmul_precision('tensorfloat32') on GPU only.

issues.title: TTS-LSTM float32 parity borderline at ~1.2e-3
issues.description: 2 float32 TTS cases exceed 1e-3 parity threshold (1.24e-3 and 1.21e-3). Caused by cuDNN LSTM vs jax.lax.scan accumulation order differences. Not a logic bug — 0.024% relative error on MOS scale 1-5.
issues.fix: Widen TTS parity tolerance to 2e-3 in tests, or investigate if cuDNN-compatible accumulation order can be replicated.

issues.title: Per-shape JIT recompilation with no static-shape cache key
issues.description: Each new (batch_size, seq_len) retraces (~0.34-0.54s CPU, ~0.3-0.7s GPU). No static-shape cache key. Variable-length batched inference pays recompile per shape.
issues.fix: Use padded static shapes with mask, or document that users should batch-pad to fixed lengths. Persistent cache (ISSUE-02) would amortize across processes.

issues.title: GPU memory pressure at bs=8/full-1300 on 8GB cards
issues.description: bs=8 at max segment length (1300) emits XLA OOM warnings on 8GB GPUs. Completes but near-limit.
issues.fix: Add automatic batch-size reduction or memory-mapped segment loading for low-memory GPUs. Document recommended batch sizes per GPU memory tier.
